cities.base: Kazanchis or the lower end of Bole, between the museums at Arat Kilo and the restaurants at Bole Medhanialem. Piazza is the atmospheric choice and the old Italian quarter, but it is rougher after dark
cities.name: Addis Ababa

cities.base: Inside Jugol itself, in one of the converted Harari houses around Feres Magala, so that the alleys and the hyena men are a walk and not a drive. The new town outside the wall has the bigger hotels and
cities.name: Harar

cities.base: Dinsho for the nyala on the lawn and the forest walks, Goba for hot water and an early start on the Sanetti road. Robe in between has the airport and the market. Dinsho Lodge is basic and cold; Goba's
cities.name: Bale Mountains, Dinsho and Goba

cities.base: No town, no beds, no fuel and no phone signal for forty kilometres. You drive on to it from Goba before dawn and come off it the same day, or you keep going down the escarpment to Bale Mountain Lodge
cities.name: Sanetti Plateau and the Harenna Forest

cities.base: On the lakeshore strip north of the Haile Resort, so the fish landing and Amora Gedel are a fifteen minute walk at six in the morning. The town centre is ten minutes inland and has the market and the
cities.name: Hawassa

cities.base: The west shore is 7 km of dirt off the Addis road and has the swimmable beaches and the easiest access; the east and south shores are quieter, better for birds, and 12 to 20 km of worse track. Either
cities.name: Lake Langano

places.name: National Museum of Ethiopia
places.note: Lucy is downstairs and the bones in the case are a cast, the real 3.2 million year old skeleton being in a vault upstairs, which nobody tells you at the door. The upper floors of Aksumite and Gondarine work are thin and badly lit; go for the hominids and leave.
places.neighborhood: Arat Kilo, King George VI Street

places.name: Ethnological Museum, Addis Ababa University
places.note: Haile Selassie's palace, so you walk through his bedroom and bathroom on the way to the best collection of Ethiopian crosses and icons in the country. Weekend hours are shorter than weekday and the ticket office closes an hour before the building does.

places.name: Adwa Victory Memorial Museum
places.note: Built in 2024 on the old stadium site to tell the 1896 defeat of Italy from the Ethiopian side, and it is loud, national and unembarrassed about it. It shuts without notice for state functions, so have a second plan for the afternoon.

places.name: Red Terror Martyrs Memorial Museum
places.note: Two rooms on the Derg killings of 1977 to 1978, with the coffins and the skulls in the open, guided by survivors who lost family. Free, forty minutes, and it will reframe every conversation you have for the rest of the trip; confirm the Sunday closure locally rather than turning up on one.

places.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral
places.note: Haile Selassie and the Empress are in marble tombs in the nave, and the churchyard holds the graves of the Ethiopian dead of the Italian occupation. On Sundays and the big saints days the whole compound is given to the liturgy and visitors are not taken round the tombs, so come midweek.

places.name: Merkato
places.note: The biggest open air market on the continent, laid out by trade, so there is a recycling quarter where oil drums become stoves and a spice quarter that smells of berbere for two blocks. Go with someone local, carry nothing in a back pocket, and accept that it is work rather than a stroll.

places.name: Entoto Maryam and the Entoto ridge
places.note: Menelik's first palace and the octagonal church he built in 1885, at 3,200 m in eucalyptus, with the whole plateau below you. Come early before the haze; the new Entoto Park next door is a manicured municipal thing and not the reason to go up.

places.name: Tomoca Coffee, Piazza
places.note: Roasting on the same site since 1953, no chairs worth the name, everyone standing at the counter with a macchiato in a glass. The beans in the paper bags behind the till are the best thing you will carry home.

places.name: Yohannis Kitfo
places.note: Gurage kitfo done properly: raw minced beef worked with spiced butter and mitmita, served leb leb if you want it barely warmed, with ayib and gomen and kocho rather than injera. On Wednesdays and Fridays the Orthodox fast means the kitchen turns vegan whether you are fasting or not.

places.name: The kurt bet butcheries at Sengatera
places.note: A butcher's shop with tables: you point at the carcass hanging behind the counter, they cut it down, and it arrives raw on a board with awaze and mustard. Fasting days are Wednesday and Friday and the meat rails are bare then, so this is a Tuesday or Saturday lunch.

places.name: Yod Abyssinia
places.note: The tourist dinner with the dance troupe working through Amhara, Tigray, Oromo and Gurage routines, and the food is better than the format deserves. Book, go once, and eat everywhere else without the show.

places.name: Topia Tej House
places.note: Tej is honey wine drunk from a berele, the round flask with the thin neck, and it goes down like juice at around eleven percent. Order the dry one, eat something first, and stop at two.

places.name: The Jugol wall circuit
places.note: Four kilometres of sixteenth century wall with five original gates, and inside it 368 alleys that are too narrow for a car and are not on any map you can follow. A licensed Harari guide is roughly USD 15 for a half day and is the difference between seeing the city and getting lost in it.

places.name: Grand Jami Mosque
places.note: Twin white minarets over the old town, the oldest fabric going back to the sixteenth century. Non-Muslims are normally shown the courtyard and not the prayer hall, and on Fridays you are not shown anything at all, so put it on any other day.

places.name: Rimbaud House
places.note: An Indian merchant's timber house of carved galleries and stained glass that Rimbaud almost certainly never lived in, now a museum to the eleven years he spent here running guns and coffee. The old photographs of Harar upstairs are the actual reason to climb them.

places.name: Harari cultural house, Adare Gar
places.note: One red carpeted room with tiered platforms, wall niches holding basketwork, and imported Chinese bowls set into the plaster, which is how every Harari family lived and several still do. Twenty minutes of looking and twenty of being told what each level of the platform meant.

places.name: Sherif Harar City Museum
places.note: A private collection of manuscripts, coins, Harari jewellery and weapons assembled by one man, better labelled than the state museums and half empty. Opening is at the owner's discretion, so send word ahead through your guide.

places.name: The hyena men outside Fallana Gate
places.note: After dark a man sits in the dirt with a basket of scraps and calls spotted hyenas by name until eight or ten of them come in off the hill and take meat from a stick in his mouth. Two families run it on opposite sides of the wall, roughly USD 8 per group plus USD 4 for the car, and it is a genuine n
places.neighborhood: Outside the eastern wall, Fallana and Argobba gates

places.name: Gidir Magala
places.note: The old meat market under a tin roof in the middle of the walled city, where the hyena men buy the scraps for the evening. Loud, wet underfoot, and the honest end of every meal you will eat here.

places.name: Mekina Girgir
places.note: One alley of treadle sewing machines going at once, which is where the name comes from, turning out the striped Harari dresses. You can have a shirt run up in a day for around USD 12 if you buy the cloth at Shoa Gate first.

places.name: Awaday khat market at first light
places.note: The largest khat market in the Horn, in full motion from 05:30 as the bundles are graded and loaded for Somaliland and Djibouti before the leaf wilts. You are there to watch the trade, not to chew, and by nine it is over.
places.neighborhood: Awaday, 15 km west on the Dire Dawa road

places.name: Babille and the Valley of Marvels
places.note: A valley of balanced granite towers on the Jijiga road, and an elephant sanctuary that holds a few hundred of an isolated desert subspecies you will very probably not see. Go for the rock and the camel caravans on the road, and treat any elephant as a bonus.
places.neighborhood: Dakhata Valley, 35 km east of Harar

places.name: Harari breakfast on Feres Magala
places.note: Fatira, a folded pancake fried with egg and eaten with honey, plus hulbat, the green fenugreek paste that comes with almost everything Harari. Three dollars for two people and it holds until the afternoon.

places.name: The coffee stalls on Feres Magala
places.note: Harar is the name on the bag for the dry processed beans from the hills around it, and the stalls on the square roast, pound and brew them in a jebena in front of you. Take the third pour, baraka, if you are offered it; leaving after the first is rude.

places.name: Dinsho park headquarters and the nyala trail
places.note: Mountain nyala graze the lawn in front of the office at dawn and dusk, along with Menelik's bushbuck and warthog, which makes it the easiest large mammal viewing in Ethiopia. Entry is a few dollars a day plus a compulsory armed scout at around USD 8, both paid in birr at the office.

places.name: The Gaysay grasslands drive
places.note: Open grass and marsh either side of the Robe road where the nyala herds come down at first light, with warthog, reedbuck and the occasional wolf crossing. Best done from a vehicle at 06:30 and finished by nine.
places.neighborhood: Gaysay, north of the Dinsho gate

places.name: Mount Gaysay
places.note: Three to four hours up and down through juniper and hagenia to a ridge that shows you the whole northern park and, on a clear morning, the Sanetti wall behind it. Steep, thin air, and you need the scout with you.

places.name: The juniper and hagenia forest above Dinsho
places.note: Old growth juniper hung with beard lichen, where the colobus sit and the Abyssinian catbird actually calls back. Flat, an hour, and the one thing here you can do in the afternoon without a car.

places.name: Web Valley
places.note: Open moorland at 3,400 m with the highest density of Ethiopian wolves anywhere, which is why the research programme keeps its base here. The track in is rough enough to need a real 4x4 and impassable in heavy rain.
places.neighborhood: Web Valley, 40 km west of Dinsho

places.name: Dinsho Lodge
places.note: The old park lodge: stone, cold, a fire in the evening and a short menu of shiro, pasta and tibs. It is the only dinner within twenty minutes of the Dinsho gate, so it is not a choice so much as a fact.

places.name: Robe market
places.note: The Oromo market town for the whole Bale plateau: grain, chillies, saddles, and the honey that Bale is actually known for, sold in old water bottles. Weekends are the full version and midweek is a quarter of it.

places.name: Goba and the Wabe Shebelle Hotel
places.note: The one hotel in Goba with a working dining room and hot water, on the site of the old imperial guest house, and the base for anyone driving the Sanetti road at dawn. The food is plain and the point is that it exists at 2,700 m.

places.name: The buna bets on Robe main street
places.note: Jebena coffee, popcorn on the side, frankincense on a coal, done a dozen times a day in every third doorway. Thirty birr and the warmest twenty minutes of a Bale morning.

places.name: Sof Omar Caves
places.note: The Web river runs straight through a limestone massif and comes out the other side, leaving fluted pillared chambers that are both a geological site and a Muslim pilgrimage one. Four hours of driving each way from Robe on a bad road, so it is a full day and only worth it if caves are your thing.
places.neighborhood: Sof Omar, 120 km east of Robe

places.name: The Goba to Dolo Mena road
places.note: The highest all weather road in Africa, climbing out of Goba onto forty kilometres of afroalpine plateau before falling 2,000 m into cloud forest. Leave Goba by 06:30: the wolves hunt early and the plateau fogs in by eleven.
places.neighborhood: Sanetti Plateau, 3,800 to 4,377 m at the road high point

places.name: Tullu Demtu
places.note: Second highest point in Ethiopia at 4,385 m, and a spur road climbs to within ten minutes of the top, which is the only reason most people ever stand on one. Get out of the car slowly; anyone who hurries the last stretch feels it.

places.name: Wolf watching on the Sanetti molerat ground
places.note: Around 250 Ethiopian wolves survive in Bale out of perhaps 500 in the world, and they hunt giant molerats on open ground where you can watch from the car for an hour. Odds on the plateau in the early morning are good but not a guarantee; Web Valley is better and harder to reach.

places.name: The Rafu lava pillars
places.note: A field of weathered basalt spires in the middle of the plateau, with everlasting flowers and lichen at your feet and nothing else for twenty kilometres. Twenty minutes of walking at 4,000 m is more work than it sounds.

places.name: The Sanetti tarns and the giant lobelia
places.note: Shallow glacial pools with wattled cranes and ruddy shelduck on them, standing between six metre lobelias that flower once and die. Frost most nights and around 10 C by day, so this is the one place in Ethiopia you want a proper jacket.

places.name: The Harenna escarpment descent
places.note: Forty switchbacks off the plateau edge, from frost and lobelia into dripping cloud forest in under an hour, which is the single most abrupt landscape change in the country. Usually in cloud; drive it anyway.

places.name: Rira village
places.note: A line of thatch and tin in a clearing where the forest people keep bees in log hives up in the trees and let their cattle graze the understorey. Stop for coffee, buy honey, and do not expect anything else.

places.name: The Manyate wild coffee walk
places.note: Coffee grows wild in the understorey here and a community run association walks you through the picking, the drying racks and a roast at the end. Roughly USD 15 per person going to the association, and it is the most convincing coffee hour in Ethiopia because nothing was planted.

places.name: Bale Mountain Lodge
places.note: The only comfortable building on the far side of the plateau, and a lunch stop that will cook for non residents if you call ahead. Rooms run well over USD 250 half board, which is another category of trip from the rest of this one.

places.name: Amora Gedel at dawn
places.note: Marabou storks, pelicans and black and white colobus in the fig trees, with vervets working the path, from about 06:15 until the sun is properly up. The whole of Hawassa jogs, prays and does aerobics along this shore at the same hour, which is half the point.

places.name: The fish landing and the grills
places.note: Boats come in from about half six, tilapia and catfish are gutted on the concrete, the heads go to the marabous standing a metre away, and the stalls behind fry the fillets while you wait. Five dollars gets you more fried fish and awaze than two people can finish.
places.neighborhood: Lake Hawassa jetty, beside Amora Gedel

places.name: The Hawassa lakeshore promenade
places.note: Four flat kilometres of paved path under fig trees between the lake and the hotels, busy from five in the evening until dark. Do not swim: the lake carries bilharzia and hippo.
places.neighborhood: Lakeshore, from Haile Resort to the jetty

places.name: Gudumale and the Sidama Monument
places.note: The open ground where Sidama assemblies are held and the monument raised to the regional statehood vote of 2019, which is recent politics rather than history. Ten minutes unless something is on, and if something is on stay and watch.

places.name: Hawassa main market
places.note: Enset leaves in stacks, green coffee by the sack, and the long handled wooden tools nobody sells in Addis any more. Sidama country runs on enset rather than grain and this is where you see it.

places.name: Sidama buna in the Piazza cafes
places.note: Sidama and Yirgacheffe are grown within two hours of this bench and the macchiatos here are better than anything in Addis for a fifth of the money. Ask for buna tetu and you will get the clay jebena rather than the machine.

places.name: Haile Resort day pass
places.note: A pool, a lawn and a lake view for around USD 12 if you are not staying, which after three days of Bale cold is a reasonable way to spend an afternoon. The restaurant is slow and the beer is cold.

places.name: The Tikur Wuha river mouth
places.note: Papyrus channels where the river enters the lake, reached by a small boat from the jetty, and the place to actually see hippo and the swamp birds rather than the marabous on the path. Roughly USD 18 for the boat for an hour and a half, negotiated at the jetty.
places.neighborhood: North east corner of Lake Hawassa

places.name: Wondo Genet hot springs
places.note: Hot water piped out of a forested hillside into two concrete pools and a row of private cubicles, above a plantation valley of colobus and turaco. The pools are municipal and crowded at weekends; take a cubicle, or come on a weekday.
places.neighborhood: Wondo Genet, 25 km east of Hawassa

places.name: Mount Tabor
places.note: Forty minutes up a dirt track behind the town for the whole lake, the Rift wall and the Shashemene road laid out below. Do it at five when the light is long and the walk down is cool.

places.name: The swim at Langano
places.note: Brown water the colour of tea from suspended sediment, and the only large Rift lake in Ethiopia free of bilharzia, so it is the one you can get into. Warm, shallow for thirty metres, and nothing like as unpleasant as the colour suggests.

places.name: Sabana Beach Resort
places.note: The most functional of the west shore places: a strip of sand, kayaks, and a kitchen that will do grilled fish and tibs on the terrace for non residents. Weekends bring half of Addis down and midweek you get it to yourself.
places.neighborhood: West shore, 7 km off the Addis road

places.name: Bishangari Lodge
places.note: Timber and thatch bungalows in old acacia on the quiet shore, with hornbills and colobus in the canopy and a proper lunch if you ring ahead. Access is 12 km of dirt off the Arsi Negele road and slow after rain.
places.neighborhood: South east shore, in the acacia forest

places.name: Hara Langano Lodge
places.note: Set back on the east side with the best sunset angle on the lake and the Arsi escarpment behind it. Birders base here; everyone else comes for dinner and the view.

places.name: Abijatta-Shalla gate and the flamingo shore
places.note: Lesser flamingo and great white pelican on a soda lake that has shrunk badly from soda ash extraction and irrigation, so the birds are sometimes two kilometres out across cracked mud. Around USD 12 entry plus a scout; ask at the gate where the water actually is before you commit the morning.
places.neighborhood: Abijatta-Shalla National Park, west of the main road

places.name: The Lake Shalla hot springs
places.note: Boiling water coming up through black sand at the edge of the deepest lake in Ethiopia, 266 m down in a collapsed caldera. People boil eggs in it, which is the whole entertainment; the drama is the crater rim behind.
places.neighborhood: North east shore of Lake Shalla

places.name: Mount Fike
places.note: The ridge between the two lakes, an hour up, and the one place you see Abijatta, Shalla and Langano at once, three lakes of three different colours. Ostrich and Grant's gazelle on the flats on the way in.

places.name: The Batu jetty on Lake Ziway
places.note: Fishermen land tilapia at a wooden jetty surrounded by marabou, pelican and a wall of jacana and kingfishers that will sit a metre from you. The photography is absurdly easy and it costs a few birr to the boys who hold the fish up.

places.name: Tulu Gudo island
places.note: A monastery island that sheltered the Ark and the Aksumite manuscripts during the ninth century invasions, reached by an open boat and a 20 minute climb. Around USD 30 for the boat split between you, and a long half day for a small church with very old books.
places.neighborhood: Lake Ziway, one hour by boat from Batu

outings.why: Out of Goba at 06:30, up onto forty kilometres of plateau at 3,800 m rising to 4,377 m at the road high point to look for Ethiopian wolves hunting molerats, the spur to Tullu Demtu, then the switchbacks down into the Harenna cloud forest fo
outings.name: The Sanetti Plateau and the Harenna descent
outings.season: All year. Worst in the July and August rains when the platea
outings.fallback: Plateau only: Goba up to Tullu Demtu and the Rafu pillars and back down, five hours, and you still get the wolves.

outings.why: Forty kilometres of track west from Dinsho onto open moorland at 3,400 m, which is where the Ethiopian Wolf Conservation Programme works because the wolf density is the highest anywhere. Better odds than Sanetti and a worse road; after rain
outings.name: Web Valley at dawn
outings.season: October to March. Avoid after heavy rain.
outings.fallback: The Gaysay grasslands drive at 06:30 for nyala and a chance of a wolf crossing, back for breakfast.

outings.why: On foot with the park scout from the headquarters through juniper and out onto the Gaysay grass, for mountain nyala, Menelik's bushbuck, warthog and colobus, at a walking pace. Flat, three hours, and the altitude is the only difficulty.
outings.name: The Gaysay grasslands walk
outings.season: All year, best at first light.
outings.fallback: The juniper forest loop behind the headquarters, one hour, which still has the colobus.

outings.why: Steep up through hagenia to a 3,543 m ridge for the whole northern park and the Sanetti wall behind it. Four hours round trip from the gate, scout compulsory, and the last section is loose.
outings.name: Mount Gaysay
outings.season: All year. Miserable in the August rain.
outings.fallback: The Dinsho nyala trail, ninety minutes, same animals and no climb.

outings.why: The Web river disappears into a limestone massif and comes out the other side, leaving pillared chambers you wade and scramble through with a local guide and a torch. Four hours of bad road each way from Robe for two or three hours undergro
outings.name: Sof Omar
outings.season: November to March. The river is too high to enter the main p
outings.fallback: Robe market and the Dinsho forest instead, which costs you nothing and no driving.

outings.why: The alleys after dark with a Harari guide, out through Fallana Gate to where a man sits in the dirt and calls spotted hyenas in off the hill by name to take meat from a stick in his mouth. Twenty minutes of hyena and an hour of city; the an
outings.name: The Jugol night walk and the hyena men
outings.fallback: The same walk in daylight, which is the alleys, Gidir Magala and Mekina Girgir without the hyenas.

outings.why: The biggest khat market in the Horn, fifteen kilometres west, running flat out from 05:30 as bundles are graded and loaded for Djibouti and Somaliland before the leaf loses its value. You are watching a commodity exchange conducted at a spr
outings.name: Awaday at first light
outings.fallback: Gidir Magala in the old city at seven, which is the same energy at a tenth of the scale.

outings.why: East on the Jijiga road into a valley of balanced granite towers, with an elephant sanctuary holding a few hundred isolated desert elephants that you will very probably not see. Half a day, hot below 1,000 m, and worth it for the rock and t
outings.name: Babille and the Valley of Marvels
outings.season: All year. Hot from March to May.
outings.fallback: The Sherif Harar City Museum and a long lunch, which is the wet weather Harar day.

outings.why: Down to the jetty for 06:15 as the boats land, the tilapia are gutted on the concrete and the marabous stand a metre off waiting for the heads, then the fig trees for colobus and the fried fish stalls for breakfast. Free, fifteen minutes on
outings.name: Amora Gedel at dawn
outings.fallback: The lakeshore promenade at five in the evening, which is the same walk with the whole town on it.

outings.why: A small open boat from the jetty up to the papyrus channels where the river enters the lake, for hippo, pelican and the swamp birds. Roughly USD 18 for the boat negotiated at the jetty, ninety minutes on the water, and there is no shade on
outings.name: The Tikur Wuha hippo boat
outings.season: All year. Windy afternoons make it unpleasant, so go early.
outings.fallback: Mount Tabor at five for the lake from above, ninety minutes on foot.

outings.why: Twenty five kilometres east and 500 m up into a forested valley where hot water comes out of the hillside into municipal pools and private cubicles, with colobus and turaco in the plantation above. The pools are crowded and not pretty; take
outings.name: Wondo Genet
outings.season: All year. Weekends are packed, so go on a weekday.
outings.fallback: The Hawassa market and the Piazza coffee houses, two hours and no driving.

outings.why: Across the main road into the park for flamingo and pelican on the Abijatta shore, then over the ridge to boiling springs at the edge of Shalla, 266 m deep in a collapsed caldera. Abijatta has shrunk badly and the birds can be two kilometre
outings.name: Abijatta-Shalla and the Shalla hot springs
outings.season: All year. Flamingo numbers are highest from November to Febr
outings.fallback: Mount Fike for the three lakes from the ridge, two hours, no gate fee argument.

outings.why: An hour at the Ziway jetty where the jacanas and pelicans sit close enough to be embarrassing, then an open boat out to the monastery island that hid the Ark and the Aksumite manuscripts in the ninth century. The boat is an hour each way wi
outings.name: The Batu jetty and Tulu Gudo
outings.season: All year. The crossing is rough in the afternoon wind, so le
outings.fallback: The jetty birds alone, one hour, which is most of the value for none of the boat.

outings.why: The recycling quarter and the spice lanes of Merkato with a local guide, then up to Piazza for Tomoca, the Italian shopfronts and lunch. It is the only way to read Addis as a city rather than a series of car parks, and Merkato needs company
outings.name: Merkato and the Piazza on foot
outings.season: All year. Merkato is a quarter of itself on Sunday.
outings.fallback: Arat Kilo on foot: the National Museum, the Ethnological Museum and Holy Trinity, all within a kilometre.

outings.why: South west on the Butajira road to Adadi Mariam, a rock hewn church cut below ground in the Lalibela manner and the only one you can currently reach without entering a do not travel region, then the field of 36 carved stelae at Tiya and the
outings.name: Tiya and Adadi Mariam
outings.season: All year. The Adadi track is poor after rain.
outings.fallback: Entoto at first light and the Ethnological Museum after, half a day and no drive.

destination.name: Ethiopia
destination.pitch: The northern circuit that most people mean by Ethiopia is under do not travel advisories and is off this itinerary, but what is left is the walled Muslim city of Harar, the Bale massif with the last Ethiopian wolves on it, and the best food
destination.caveat: As of September 2026 the US, UK and Canada all advise against all travel to the Amhara region, which means Lalibela, Gondar, Bahir Dar and the Simien Mountains, and to Tigray, which means Axum, so the rock hewn churches and the northern historic route are out and this pack routes east to Harar and s Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Addis is 3.5 million people at 2,355 m with the best museums in the region and the worst traffic, and is a place to eat and to understand the country rather than to look at.
because.food: Injera with a dozen wots on it, kitfo worked raw with spiced butter, tere siga cut off the carcass in the butcher's shop, and a vegan fasting platter on Wednesdays and Fridays that is the best accidental vegetarian food anywhere; the coffee
because.nature: Bale holds around 250 of the roughly 500 Ethiopian wolves left alive, the largest afroalpine plateau in Africa at 4,000 m, and a cloud forest on the far side of it, all of it reachable on one road in a day.
because.culture: Harar is a living UNESCO walled city of 82 mosques where the hyena feeding is a nightly habit rather than a performance, and Addis carries the Derg, the Adwa victory and the whole Orthodox liturgical year without packaging any of it.
because.adventure: The Goba to Dolo Mena road is the highest all weather road on the continent, Web Valley needs a real 4x4 and good weather, and Sof Omar is a river running straight through a mountain.
because.relaxation: Langano is the one large Rift lake you can swim in and Wondo Genet is a hot spring in a forest, but nothing here is a beach holiday and Bale is genuinely cold.
because.exploration: Six ecosystems and four languages inside twelve days, from a 2,355 m capital to a sixteenth century walled city that traded with India, to frost and giant lobelia, to soda lakes with flamingos on them.
